N1 closure is empirical, not just by construction: my probe builds fixture copies of both sound folders under measure/runs/audio_game_integration_20261014/, patches a copy of the script to point at the fixtures, and shows that a symlink to /etc/hostname in both folders (scenario A) or in the demo folder only (scenario B) exits 1 with 'symlink in <dir>: tap.ogg' and creates no output folder; an extra 15th name (C) and a case-changed TAP.ogg (D) both exit 1 on the inventory allowlist with no output folder; a clean fixture run (E) exits 0 with 17 entries and sha256sum -c passing, proving the patched copy is faithful. No live edit of demo/public or sounds/ occurred, and the fixture was deleted afterwards. On the real folders: the allowlist cannot be bypassed by a path separator (readdirSync returns bare names and the sorted join-compare rejects anything outside APPROVED) or a case change (verified in scenario D); rm -rf scope is unchanged (constant HANDOFF, and every pre-write die happens before rmSync); --help exits 0 and any argument exits 1 with one usage line; the regenerated folder holds the 14 files plus the three metadata files with no /home/ path and no user name (both greps exit 1); and the monorepo status is unchanged. The committed gates pass: 5 default cases, 10 of 10 with AUDIO_HANDOFF_ARTIFACTS=1, and the adversarial allowlist pin passes 1 of 1; tsc stays at the 51-error baseline through the heavy runner.

The delta holds 91ad6b8a and 098decd4 (Red r1 cases), 5b60488e (Red r1 record), a0cdaf4f (Green), and df7f01bf (plan evidence).

Allowlist strength: APPROVED is a constant of 14 lowercase names; both folders must list exactly it after sorting, so a path-separator name cannot reach a join (readdirSync yields bare names and any such name would fail the compare anyway), a case change fails (scenario D), and a 15th file fails (scenario C). The format check inside the copy loop is now unreachable defense in depth because only .ogg and .mp3 names can pass the allowlist.

Write scope and failure atomicity: every die before rmSync(HANDOFF) — unreadable dir, symlink, bad inventory, byte mismatch — leaves any previous hand-off untouched, and the fixture probe confirms failing runs create no output folder at all; rmSync targets only the constant HANDOFF under out/; the manifests are written only after all 14 copies and hashes.
